passages.text: And Elihu went on to say: “Do you think this is just? You say, ‘I am more righteous than God.’
passages.sermon:
Elihu spoke.
Elihu addressed Job.
Elihu asked Job a question.
Elihu said, "Do you think this is justice?"
Elihu said, "You claim you are more righteous than God."
passages.original: וַיַּ֥עַן אֱלִיה֗וּ וַיֹּאמַֽר׃ הֲ֭זֹאת חָשַׁ֣בְתָּ לְמִשְׁפָּ֑ט אָ֝מַ֗רְתָּ צִדְקִ֥י מֵאֵֽל׃

passages.text: For you ask, ‘What does it profit me, and what benefit do I gain apart from sin?’
passages.sermon:
Job speaks to God.
Job asks a question.
Job says, “What profit do I have?”
Job says, “What benefit do I gain if I do not sin?”
passages.original: כִּֽי־ תֹ֭אמַר מַה־ יִּסְכָּן־ לָ֑ךְ מָֽה־ אֹ֝עִ֗יל מֵֽחַטָּאתִֽי׃

passages.text: I will reply to you and to your friends as well.
passages.sermon: Elihu spoke to Job and his friends.\r\nElihu said, "I will answer you, Job."\r\nI will also answer your friends."
passages.original: אֲ֭נִי אֲשִֽׁיבְךָ֣ מִלִּ֑ין וְֽאֶת־ רֵעֶ֥יךָ עִמָּֽךְ׃

passages.text: Look to the heavens and see; gaze at the clouds high above you.
passages.sermon:
Look at the heavens.
See them above you.
Look at the clouds.
The clouds are high above you.
passages.original: הַבֵּ֣ט שָׁמַ֣יִם וּרְאֵ֑ה וְשׁ֥וּר שְׁ֝חָקִ֗ים גָּבְה֥וּ מִמֶּֽךָּ׃

passages.text: If you sin, what do you accomplish against Him? If you multiply your transgressions, what do you do to Him?
passages.sermon:
God is above you.
God is greater than you.
If you sin, you do not harm God.
If you commit many wrongs, you do not affect God.
passages.original: אִם־ חָ֭טָאתָ מַה־ תִּפְעָל־ בּ֑וֹ וְרַבּ֥וּ פְ֝שָׁעֶ֗יךָ מַה־ תַּעֲשֶׂה־ לּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: If you are righteous, what do you give Him, or what does He receive from your hand?
passages.sermon:
God is your Creator.
God is above you.
If you are righteous, you do not give anything to God.
God does not receive anything from your hand.
passages.original: אִם־ צָ֭דַקְתָּ מַה־ תִּתֶּן־ ל֑וֹ א֥וֹ מַה־ מִיָּדְךָ֥ יִקָּֽח׃

passages.text: Your wickedness affects only a man like yourself, and your righteousness only a son of man.
passages.sermon:
Your wickedness affects people like you.
Your wickedness does not affect God.
Your righteousness benefits only other human beings.
Your righteousness does not benefit God.
You are a human.
Your actions touch other humans, not God.
passages.original: לְאִישׁ־ כָּמ֥וֹךָ רִשְׁעֶ֑ךָ וּלְבֶן־ אָ֝דָ֗ם צִדְקָתֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: Men cry out under great oppression; they plead for relief from the arm of the mighty.
passages.sermon:
People suffer under great oppression.
They cry out because they are mistreated.
They plead for help from the power of the strong.
The strong use their power to oppress others.
The oppressed ask for relief from this power.
passages.original: מֵ֭רֹב עֲשׁוּקִ֣ים יַזְעִ֑יקוּ יְשַׁוְּע֖וּ מִזְּר֣וֹעַ רַבִּֽים׃

passages.text: But no one asks, ‘Where is God my Maker, who gives us songs in the night, who teaches us more than the beasts of the earth and makes us wiser than the birds of the air?’
passages.sermon:
God is our Maker.
God gives us songs in the night.
God teaches us more than the beasts of the earth.
God makes us wiser than the birds of the air.
But no one asks, "Where is God my Maker?"
passages.original: וְֽלֹא־ אָמַ֗ר אַ֭יֵּה אֱל֣וֹהַּ עֹשָׂ֑י נֹתֵ֖ן זְמִר֣וֹת בַּלָּֽיְלָה׃ מַ֭לְּפֵנוּ מִבַּהֲמ֣וֹת אָ֑רֶץ וּמֵע֖וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם יְחַכְּמֵֽנוּ׃

passages.text: There they cry out, but He does not answer, because of the pride of evil men.
passages.sermon: People cry out in that place.\r\nGod does not answer them.\r\nHe does not answer because evil men are proud.
passages.original: שָׁ֣ם יִ֭צְעֲקוּ וְלֹ֣א יַעֲנֶ֑ה מִ֝פְּנֵ֗י גְּא֣וֹן רָעִֽים׃

passages.text: Surely God does not listen to empty pleas, and the Almighty does not take note of it.
passages.sermon: God is the Creator and Almighty.\r\nGod does not listen to empty pleas.\r\nThe Almighty does not pay attention to them.
passages.original: אַךְ־ שָׁ֭וְא לֹא־ יִשְׁמַ֥ע׀ אֵ֑ל וְ֝שַׁדַּ֗י לֹ֣א יְשׁוּרֶֽנָּה׃

passages.text: How much less, then, when you say that you do not see Him, that your case is before Him and you must wait for Him, and further, that in His anger He has not punished or taken much notice of folly!
passages.sermon:
Elihu speaks to Job.
Elihu says that Job claims he cannot see God.
Job says his case is before God.
Job says he must wait for God.
Elihu says God has not shown His anger.
God has not punished much.
God has not paid much attention to foolishness.
passages.original: אַ֣ף כִּֽי־ תֹ֭אמַר לֹ֣א תְשׁוּרֶ֑נּוּ דִּ֥ין לְ֝פָנָ֗יו וּתְח֥וֹלֵֽל לֽוֹ׃ וְעַתָּ֗ה כִּי־ אַ֭יִן פָּקַ֣ד אַפּ֑וֹ וְלֹֽא־ יָדַ֖ע בַּפַּ֣שׁ מְאֹֽד׃

passages.text: So Job opens his mouth in vain and multiplies words without knowledge.”
passages.sermon:
Job is a man who speaks now.
Job opens his mouth for no good reason.
Job speaks without knowledge.
Job says many words.
Job does not understand what he says.
passages.original: וְ֭אִיּוֹב הֶ֣בֶל יִפְצֶה־ פִּ֑יהוּ בִּבְלִי־ דַ֝֗עַת מִלִּ֥ין יַכְבִּֽר׃פ
